summary: Plan for cohomological modular symbols and analytic p-adic L-functions, extending Tau Ceti ModularForms under accepted RS-08. The packet retains the Hom-side symbols, signed periods, small-slope and critical-slope single-form constructions and the worked ordinary and supersingular examples. It adds the rational Drinfeld–Manin retraction assigned by the Nakamura extraction, with a separating-annihilator theorem, a usable projection API, rational and integral-obstruction tests, and explicit higher-weight and realization boundaries. The pass is partial: L4 coefficient embeddings and primitive/imprimitive level changes, source closure for the new general-weight splitting, and the full typed suggested interfaces remain open.

nodes.title: Modular symbols
nodes.statement: For Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index and a right ℤ[Γ]-module V, Symb_Γ(V) is the group of additive maps φ : Δ₀ → V with φ(γD) = φ(D)|γ^{-1} for all γ ∈ Γ, D ∈ Δ₀, where Δ₀ = Div⁰(P¹(ℚ)) is the degree-zero divisor module with its action of GL₂⁺(ℚ) by linear fractional transformations (imported from ModularForms Layer 8, see requests). In the formal version V carries the left representation ρ(γ)v = v|γ^{-1}, and the condition reads φ(γD) = ρ(γ)φ(D); equivalently Symb_Γ(V) = Hom_{ℤ[Γ]}(Δ₀, V).
hypotheses: Γ acts on Δ₀ through SL₂(ℤ) → GL₂(ℚ).
Left/right conventions: Pollack–Stevens' right action v|γ is recorded as the left representation v ↦ v|γ^{-1}.
proofSteps: Define symbols Γ ρ as the additive subgroup of maps Δ₀ → V satisfying the equivariance; closure under sums and negatives is immediate.
A modular symbol is determined by its values on the unimodular divisors {γ0} − {γ∞}, because these generate Δ₀ (Manin's theorem, imported from ModularForms Layer 8).
acceptance: Symb_{SL₂(ℤ)}(ℤ) = 0: by the Manin relations φ({0} − {∞}) = v satisfies 2v = 0 and 3v = 0.
Symb_{Γ₀(11)}(ℤ) has rank 3 = 2g + (c − 1), with genus g = 1 and c = 2 cusps.
When the orders of torsion elements act invertibly on V, Symb_Γ(V) ≅ H¹_c(H/Γ, Ṽ) (Pollack–Stevens, citing Ash–Stevens [2, Prop. 4.2]); planned as remaining work.

nodes.title: ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)] is free over ℤ[Γ]
nodes.statement: For Γ ≤ G of finite index in a group G (here G = SL₂(ℤ) or PSL₂(ℤ)), ℤ[G] is a free left ℤ[Γ]-module with basis any set of right coset representatives {g_j} of Γ\G; consequently Hom_{ℤ[Γ]}(ℤ[G], V) ≅ ∏_j V by F ↦ (F(g_j))_j.
hypotheses: Γ acts by left multiplication through the inclusion.
proofSteps: SL₂(ℤ) = ⊔_i Γ g_i gives ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)] = ⊕_i ℤ[Γ]g_i, and γ g_i ↦ (γ, i) is a bijection Γ × (Γ\SL₂(ℤ)) → SL₂(ℤ).
acceptance: For finite index the basis is finite, of size [SL₂(ℤ) : Γ].
Combined with the Manin relations this gives the ℤ[Γ]-presentation of Δ₀ by coset generators.

nodes.title: Hecke operators on modular symbols
nodes.statement: For V with a right Σ₀(N)-action extending its Γ₀(N)-action, and φ ∈ Symb_{Γ₀(N)}(V): (φ|δ)(D) := φ(δD)|δ; for a prime ℓ ∤ N, φ|T_ℓ := φ|(ℓ 0; 0 1) + Σ_{a=0}^{ℓ−1} φ|(1 a; 0 ℓ); for q | N, φ|U_q := Σ_{a=0}^{q−1} φ|(1 a; 0 q). These preserve Symb_{Γ₀(N)}(V) and commute.
hypotheses: V's Γ₀(N)-action is the restriction of the Σ₀(N)-action.

The suggested coefficient action is a monoid homomorphism from the opposite matrix semigroup to module endomorphisms, and its restriction is ρ(γ⁻¹). Preservation and commutativity apply to equivariant symbols, not arbitrary divisor maps.
proofSteps: The listed matrices are representatives of Γ₀(N)\Γ₀(N)(ℓ 0; 0 1)Γ₀(N) (resp. for U_q); right multiplication by γ ∈ Γ₀(N) permutes the cosets, so Σ φ|α_i is again Γ₀(N)-invariant.

The operators come from an action of the Γ₀(N) Hecke ring of double cosets on Symb_{Γ₀(N)}(V), with T_ℓ the class of Γ₀(N)(ℓ 0; 0 1)Γ₀(N); commutativity follows from commutativity of that ring (Tau Ceti HeckeRing.GL2.commRingHeckeRingGamma0).

nodes.title: Modular symbols as functions on cosets (Manin symbols, cohomological side)
nodes.statement: Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index, let {g_j} be right coset representatives of Γ\SL₂(ℤ), and let V be a right ℤ[Γ]-module. For g ∈ SL₂(ℤ) write g = γ_g g_{j(g)} with γ_g ∈ Γ. The map φ ↦ (v_j)_j, v_j := φ({g_j 0} − {g_j ∞}), is an isomorphism from Symb_Γ(V) onto the families (v_j) ∈ ∏_j V such that, for every j, with x(g) := v_{j(g)}|γ_g^{-1}: x(g_j) + x(g_j σ) = 0, x(g_j) + x(g_j τ) + x(g_j τ²) = 0, and x(g_j) = x(−g_j), where σ = (0 −1; 1 0) and τ = (0 −1; 1 −1).
hypotheses: Γ has finite index in SL₂(ℤ).
The relation list is the image of Manin's kernel ℤ[G](1 + σ) + ℤ[G](1 + τ + τ²) + ℤ[G](1 − (−1)) under the coset basis.
proofSteps: By Manin's theorem (requested from ModularForms Layer 8) d : ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)] → Δ₀, g ↦ {g0} − {g∞}, is surjective with kernel the left ideal I generated by 1 + σ, 1 + τ + τ² and 1 − (−1); so Symb_Γ(V) = Hom_{ℤ[Γ]}(ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)]/I, V).
A ℤ[Γ]-linear map F : ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)] → V is determined by the values F(g_j) on the coset basis (coset-basis), with F(γ g_j) = F(g_j)|γ^{-1}.
F kills I iff F(g(1 + σ)) = F(g(1 + τ + τ²)) = F(g(1 − (−1))) = 0 for every g; by Γ-equivariance it suffices to take g = g_j, and F(g) = x(g) by the first step.
Hence evaluation at the unimodular divisors d(g_j) identifies Symb_Γ(V) with the stated set of families.
acceptance: For Γ = SL₂(ℤ) (one coset, g₁ = 1) and V = ℤ with trivial action the conditions read 2v = 0 and 3v = 0, so Symb_{SL₂(ℤ)}(ℤ) = 0.
For Γ = Γ₀(11) (12 cosets) and V = ℤ the solution module has rank 3, matching Pollack's worked Γ₀(11) example.
Changing the coset representatives changes the isomorphism by the corresponding γ-twists and not its image.

nodes.title: A modular symbol is determined by its values on the fundamental-domain generators
nodes.statement: Let Γ ⊊ PSL₂(ℤ) have finite index and contain T = (1 1; 0 1), and let D₁, …, D_t, D_∞, D′₁, …, D′_s, D″₁, …, D″_r be the generators of Δ₀ read off a Farey fundamental domain, with the matrices γ_i, γ′_i (order 2) and γ″_i (order 3) in Γ (Pollack–Stevens §§2.4–2.5; the presentation is imported from ModularForms Layer 8). For a right Γ-module V and v₁, …, v_t, v_∞, v′₁, …, v′_s, v″₁, …, v″_r ∈ V with v_∞|Δ = Σ_i v_i|(1 − γ_i) − Σ_i v′_i − Σ_i v″_i (Δ := T − 1), v′_i|(1 + γ′_i) = 0 and v″_i|(1 + γ″_i + γ″_i²) = 0, there is a unique φ ∈ Symb_Γ(V) with φ(D_i) = v_i, φ(D_∞) = v_∞, φ(D′_i) = v′_i and φ(D″_i) = v″_i; every φ arises so. This is Pollack–Stevens' Corollaries 2.7 and 2.10 with the sign of the D_∞ relation corrected (sourceIssues E1).
hypotheses: Γ has finite index in PSL₂(ℤ), contains T and is proper (for the three-torsion version); for Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) apply it to the image Γ̄ and to V^{⟨−1⟩∩Γ}, since −1 acts trivially on Δ₀.
The relations among the generators are Σ_i (γ_i^{-1} − 1)D_i + Σ_i D′_i + Σ_i D″_i = (1 − T^{-1})D_∞, (1 + γ′_i)D′_i = 0 and (1 + γ″_i + γ″_i²)D″_i = 0.
proofSteps: Theorem 2.6/2.9 of Pollack–Stevens, as corrected (request to ModularForms Layer 8): Δ₀ is generated over ℤ[Γ] by the D's with the displayed relations. The relation is derived from the printed boundary relation (1 − T^{-1})e_∞ + Σ(1 − γ_i^{-1})e_i + Σ e′_i ∈ J on p. 11 by applying ∂, with D′_i = −∂(e′_i).
A ℤ[Γ]-linear map out of a presented module is the same as values on the generators satisfying the relations.

Apply φ(γD) = φ(D)|γ^{-1} to the first relation: Σ v_i|(γ_i − 1) + Σ v′_i + Σ v″_i = v_∞ − v_∞|T = −v_∞|Δ; the torsion relations give v′_i|(1 + γ′_i) = 0 and v″_i|(1 + γ″_i + γ″_i²) = 0 because γ′_i, γ″_i have order 2, 3 in PSL₂(ℤ).
acceptance: Γ₀(2) (t = 0, s = 1, F the ideal triangle with vertices −1, 0, ∞, γ′₁ = (1 1; −2 −1)): D′₁ = (1 − T^{-1})D_∞ = {0} − {−1}; with the printed sign the relation would force 2D′₁ = 0 in the torsion-free Δ₀.
Γ₀(11) with V = V_k: the relation matches Pollack's worked example (1 − (1 −1; 0 1))({0} − {∞}) + Σ(1 − γ)D = 0 (AWS notes, footnote 10), whose γ is Pollack–Stevens' γ_i^{-1}.
For V = ℚ with trivial action the conditions reduce to Σ_i v′_i + Σ_i v″_i = 0 and v′_i = v″_i = 0 (2, 3 invertible), so dim Symb_Γ(ℚ) = t + 1.

nodes.title: Boundary symbols
nodes.statement: For Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index and a right ℤ[Γ]-module V, BSymb_Γ(V) := Hom_{ℤ[Γ]}(ℤ[P¹(ℚ)], V), the maps ψ : P¹(ℚ) → V with ψ(γc) = ψ(c)|γ^{-1}. Restriction along Δ₀ ⊆ ℤ[P¹(ℚ)] gives res : BSymb_Γ(V) → Symb_Γ(V), whose image Eis_Γ(V) is the module of Eisenstein (boundary) symbols. Choosing representatives c₁, …, c_ν of the finitely many cusps Γ\P¹(ℚ) gives BSymb_Γ(V) ≅ ⊕_j V^{Γ_{c_j}}, ψ ↦ (ψ(c_j))_j, where Γ_c is the stabiliser of c.

nodes.statement: For φ ∈ Symb_Γ(V) (V with the left representation ρ(γ)v = v|γ^{-1}) and a base cusp x ∈ P¹(ℚ), c_φ(γ) := φ({γx} − {x}) is a 1-cocycle of Γ with values in (V, ρ); its class δ(φ) ∈ H¹(Γ, V) does not depend on x, and δ : Symb_Γ(V) → H¹(Γ, V) is ℤ-linear. nodes.title: The boundary exact sequence for modular symbols
nodes.statement: For Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index and any right ℤ[Γ]-module V the sequence 0 → V^Γ → BSymb_Γ(V) → Symb_Γ(V) → H¹(Γ, V) → ⊕_{c ∈ Γ\P¹(ℚ)} H¹(Γ_c, V) is exact, where the first map sends v to the constant function, the second is res, the third is δ (symbols-to-cohomology) and the last is the product of the restrictions to the cusp stabilisers (choosing representatives).
hypotheses: No invertibility hypothesis: the sequence is exact integrally.

Ext⁰ = Hom_Γ gives V^Γ, BSymb_Γ(V) and Symb_Γ(V); Ext¹_{ℤ[Γ]}(ℤ, V) = H¹(Γ, V) (groupCohomologyIsoExt).
ℤ[P¹(ℚ)] = ⊕_c ℤ[Γ/Γ_c] = ⊕_c Ind_{Γ_c}^Γ ℤ, so Ext¹_{ℤ[Γ]}(ℤ[P¹(ℚ)], V) = ⊕_c Ext¹_{ℤ[Γ_c]}(ℤ, V) = ⊕_c H¹(Γ_c, V) (Shapiro/Eckmann), and the map from H¹(Γ, V) is restriction.

nodes.title: Descent of modular symbols from a normal subgroup
nodes.statement: Let Γ′ ⊴ Γ be finite-index subgroups of SL₂(ℤ) and V a right ℤ[Γ]-module. Then Γ/Γ′ acts on Symb_{Γ′}(V) by φ ↦ φ|γ, and Symb_Γ(V) = Symb_{Γ′}(V)^{Γ/Γ′}, integrally and with no division. If [Γ : Γ′] is invertible on V, then restriction gives H¹(Γ, V) ≅ H¹(Γ′, V)^{Γ/Γ′} and H¹_par(Γ, V) ≅ H¹_par(Γ′, V)^{Γ/Γ′}, and Symb_Γ(V) is a direct summand of Symb_{Γ′}(V) via the averaging idempotent e = [Γ:Γ′]^{-1} Σ_{γ ∈ Γ/Γ′} (·)|γ.

nodes.title: Hecke operators on Γ₁(N)-symbols
nodes.statement: For V a right module over the monoid Σ₁(N) generated by Γ₁(N), Γ₀(N) and the matrices (1 a; 0 ℓ), (ℓ 0; 0 1) with (ℓ, N) = 1 (inside Σ₀(N)), and φ ∈ Symb_{Γ₁(N)}(V): for a prime ℓ ∤ N, φ|T_ℓ := Σ_{a=0}^{ℓ−1} φ|(1 a; 0 ℓ) + φ|σ_ℓ(ℓ 0; 0 1), and for q | N, φ|U_q := Σ_{a=0}^{q−1} φ|(1 a; 0 q). These preserve Symb_{Γ₁(N)}(V), commute with each other and with the diamond operators, and restrict to the Γ₀(N) operators of hecke-operators on Symb_{Γ₀(N)}(V).
hypotheses: σ_ℓ ∈ Γ₀(N) has lower-right entry ≡ ℓ mod N (so σ_ℓ(ℓ 0; 0 1) ∈ Δ¹ₗ(N)), as in the double-coset decomposition Δ^ℓ_1(N) = ⊔ Γ₁(N)σ_a(a b; 0 d).
On Symb_{Γ₀(N)}(V), σ_ℓ acts trivially and T_ℓ reduces to the Γ₀(N) formula.

Commutativity: the Hecke ring R(Δ₁(N), Γ₁(N)) is commutative (Wiese Corollary 7.14; Tau Ceti's Γ₀(N) Hecke ring for the Γ₀ case), and φ ↦ φ|T is a ring antihomomorphism from it, hence a homomorphism on a commutative ring.

nodes.title: Hom-side symbols are the dual of homological symbols
nodes.statement: For finite-index Γ, a left ℤ[Γ]-module W, and an abelian group M with trivial action, give Hom_ℤ(W, M) the right action (f|γ)(w) = f(γw). Then Symb_Γ(Hom_ℤ(W, M)) ≅ Hom_ℤ((Δ₀ ⊗ W)_Γ, M), φ ↦ ([D ⊗ w] ↦ φ(D)(w)), naturally in W and M. If W is a left module over a monoid Σ ⊇ Γ (Σ₀(N), Σ₁(N) or GL₂⁺(ℚ) ∩ M₂(ℤ)), the Hecke operator Σ_i φ|δ_i corresponds to precomposition with the operator [D ⊗ w] ↦ Σ_i [δ_i D ⊗ δ_i w] on the coinvariants, and likewise for ⟨d⟩ and ι. With W = Sym^{k}(ℤ²) this identifies Symb_Γ(Hom(Sym^k ℤ², M)) with the ℤ-dual (with values in M) of ModularForms Layer 8's module 𝕄, transposing its Hecke operators.
hypotheses: (Δ₀ ⊗ W)_Γ is the Γ-coinvariants of the diagonal action; Layer 8 uses Γ = Γ₁(N) and W = Sym^{k−2}(ℤ²).
The Hecke identification needs the same coset representatives δ_i on both sides; the transpose reverses composition, and commutativity of the Hecke algebra makes this harmless.
proofSteps: Tensor–hom adjunction: Hom_ℤ(Δ₀ ⊗ W, M) ≅ Hom_ℤ(Δ₀, Hom_ℤ(W, M)).
Γ-invariant maps on the left correspond to Γ-equivariant maps on the right (coinvariants are left adjoint to the trivial-module functor, Rep.coinvariantsAdjunction; Rep.coinvariantsTensor).
For the Hecke operators, (φ|δ)(D)(w) = (φ(δD)|δ)(w) = φ(δD)(δw), so φ|T evaluated on [D ⊗ w] is φ evaluated on Σ_i [δ_iD ⊗ δ_iw].
acceptance: For W = ℤ trivial and M = ℤ: Symb_Γ(ℤ) = Hom((Δ₀)_Γ, ℤ).
For Γ₀(11), W = ℤ: rank (Δ₀)_Γ = 3 = rank Symb_{Γ₀(11)}(ℤ).
Torsion in 𝕄 is invisible after Hom(−, ℤ) but visible for M = ℚ/ℤ.

nodes.title: The invariant pairing between V_k and Sym^k
nodes.statement: Let W_k(R) = R[X, Y]_k with the left action (γ·Q)(X, Y) = Q((X, Y)γ) and V_k(R) the same module with the right action (P|γ)(X, Y) = P((X, Y)γ*), γ* = adj γ (polynomial-coefficients). If k! is invertible in R there is a unique R-bilinear pairing ⟨ , ⟩ : V_k(R) × W_k(R) → R with ⟨(uX + vY)^k, (sX + tY)^k⟩ = (ut − vs)^k for all u, v, s, t ∈ R; on monomials ⟨X^iY^{k−i}, X^jY^{k−j}⟩ = (−1)^{k−i}/C(k, i) if i + j = k and 0 otherwise. It is perfect and satisfies ⟨P|γ, Q⟩ = ⟨P, γ·Q⟩ for every integral γ with det γ ≠ 0; so P ↦ ⟨P, ·⟩ is an isomorphism of right modules V_k(R) ≅ Hom_R(W_k(R), R). Over ℤ the pairing takes values in ℤ[1/k!] and is not integral for k ≥ 2.
hypotheses: k! ∈ R^× for the pairing to exist on all of V_k(R) × W_k(R); no determinant twist appears.
The integral comparison of Symb_Γ(V_k(ℤ)) with Hom(𝕄, ℤ) goes through the divided-power lattice and belongs to L1's integral-lattice work.
proofSteps: Write ℓ_a(X, Y) = a₁X + a₂Y; then P|γ turns ℓ_a^k into ℓ_{γ*a}^k and γ·Q turns ℓ_b^k into ℓ_{γb}^k.
det(γ*a | b) = det(γ*)·det(a | γ*^{-1}b) = det γ · det(a | γb)/det γ = det(a | γb), so the formula is invariant.

Expanding both sides in monomials forces ⟨X^iY^{k−i}, X^{k−i}Y^{i}⟩·C(k, i)² = C(k, i)(−1)^{k−i}, giving the stated values; they span when k! is invertible, and the matrix is anti-diagonal with unit entries, so the pairing is perfect.
acceptance: k = 1: ⟨uX + vY, sX + tY⟩ = ut − vs, the determinant pairing.
k = 2: ⟨XY, XY⟩ = −1/2, so the pairing is not integral.
Invariance check with γ = (1 1; 0 1), k = 2, P = X², Q = Y².

nodes.title: The period symbol of a cusp form
nodes.statement: For k ≥ 0, Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index and f ∈ S_{k+2}(Γ), ψ_f : Δ₀ → V_k(ℂ) is the additive map with ψ_f({s} − {r}) = 2πi ∫_r^s f(z)(zX + Y)^k dz (geodesic path in H, improper at cusps). Then ψ_f ∈ Symb_Γ(V_k(ℂ)), f ↦ ψ_f is ℂ-linear, ψ_{f|δ} relates to ψ_f|δ for the weight-(k+2) slash action f|δ = det(δ)^{k+1}(cz + d)^{−k−2}f(δz), so ψ_{T f} = ψ_f|T for T_ℓ, U_q and ⟨d⟩. Under polynomial-duality and symbols-coinvariants-duality, ⟨ψ_f(D), Q⟩ = 2πi · periodMap′(f)(D ⊗ w·Q) with w = (0 1; −1 0), i.e. ψ_f is Layer 8's period map transported to the Hom side.
hypotheses: Convergence at cusps: f is a cusp form (exponential decay at every cusp); this analytic input is Layer 8's convergence milestone.
Orientation: {s} − {r} is the path from r to s; Layer 8's rawPairing integrates {α, β} from β to α.
proofSteps: Well defined on Δ₀: additivity over paths (path independence of holomorphic integrals in H) makes the value on {s} − {r} consistent with the relations of Δ₀.
Γ-invariance: substituting z = γu gives ∫_{γr}^{γs} f(z)(zX + Y)^k dz = ∫_r^s f(u)(u X + Y)^k|γ^{-1} du, i.e. ψ_f(γD) = ψ_f(D)|γ^{-1}.
Hecke equivariance: the same substitution for δ ∈ Σ₀(N) gives ψ_{f|δ}(D) = ψ_f(δD)|δ; summing over coset representatives.

Comparison with Layer 8: ⟨(zX + Y)^k, Q⟩ = (w·Q)(z, 1) with w = (0 1; −1 0), as one checks on Q = (sX + tY)^k where both sides equal (tz − s)^k; so pairing ψ_f with Q is 2πi times Layer 8's rawPairing on D ⊗ w·Q.

nodes.title: Dimension of parabolic cohomology
nodes.statement: Let K be a field of characteristic 0 and Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index μ in PSL₂(ℤ) (index of the image) with trivial stabilisers in H (e.g. Γ₁(N), N ≥ 4), with ν∞ cusps. Then dim_K H¹(Γ, V_k(K)) = (k + 1)μ/6 + δ_{k,0} and dim_K H¹_par(Γ, V_k(K)) = (k + 1)μ/6 − ν∞ + 2δ_{k,0}.
hypotheses: Characteristic 0 (the computation of T-invariants and coinvariants of V_k needs k!N to be invertible).
Trivial stabilisers, so Coind(V_k) has no invariants for the finite subgroups ⟨σ⟩, ⟨τ⟩ beyond those computed by Mayer–Vietoris.
proofSteps: M = Coind_Γ^{PSL₂(ℤ)} V_k(K) has dimension (k + 1)μ; H¹(Γ, V_k) = H¹(PSL₂(ℤ), M) (Shapiro).
Mayer–Vietoris for PSL₂(ℤ) = ⟨σ⟩ ∗ ⟨τ⟩: 0 → M^G → M^{⟨σ⟩} ⊕ M^{⟨τ⟩} → M → H¹(G, M) → 0, with M^{⟨σ⟩} and M^{⟨τ⟩} of dimensions μ(k+1)/2 and μ(k+1)/3 when the stabilisers are trivial.
dim V_k(K)^Γ = δ_{k,0} and, at each cusp, dim H¹(⟨T^n⟩, V_k(K)) = dim V_k(K)^{⟨T^n⟩} = 1 (Wiese Lemma 4.15).
Combine with the exact row 0 → H¹_par → H¹ → ⊕_cusps H¹(Γ_c, V) → V_Γ → 0 of Wiese Proposition 4.14.
acceptance: Γ₁(5) (μ = 12, ν∞ = 4): k = 0 gives dim H¹_par = 0 (X₁(5) has genus 0); k = 2 gives dim H¹_par = 2 = 2·dim S₄(Γ₁(5)).
The formula equals 2 dim S_{k+2}(Γ) by the dimension formula (request to ModularForms 10C), the input for Eichler–Shimura.

nodes.title: The Eichler–Shimura isomorphism
nodes.statement: Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) be of finite index and k ≥ 0. The map S_{k+2}(Γ) ⊕ \overline{S_{k+2}(Γ)} → H¹_par(Γ, V_k(ℂ)), (f, \bar g) ↦ δ(ψ_f) + \overline{δ(ψ_g)}, is an isomorphism compatible with the Hecke and diamond operators; for each sign ±, f ↦ δ((1 ± ι)ψ_f) is an isomorphism S_{k+2}(Γ) ≅ H¹_par(Γ, V_k(ℂ))^± when ι normalises Γ. Via symbols-mod-eisenstein the same holds for Symb_Γ(V_k(ℂ))/Eis_Γ(V_k(ℂ)).
hypotheses: For Γ = Γ₁(N), N ≥ 4 (trivial stabilisers) this is Wiese Theorem 6.15; general Γ follows by symbols-level-descent from Γ ∩ Γ₁(M), M ≥ 4, over ℂ.
Uses the positive definite Petersson product on cusp forms (Tau Ceti CuspForm.peterssonInnerCosets_definite) and the dimension formula for S_{k+2}(Γ₁(N)) (request to ModularForms 10C).
proofSteps: Well defined and parabolic: δ(ψ_f) is a cocycle whose restriction to every cusp stabiliser is a coboundary (Wiese Propositions 6.7, 6.9).

Injective: the cup product and the invariant pairing on V_k give a pairing on H¹_par (Wiese Proposition 6.13, 6 invertible) which evaluates on (δψ_f, \overline{δψ_f}) to a nonzero multiple of the Petersson norm of f (Proposition 6.14); positivity of the Petersson norm forces f = 0; likewise for \bar g.
Dimensions: dim H¹_par(Γ₁(N), V_k(ℂ)) = (k + 1)μ/6 − ν∞ + 2δ_{k,0} (parabolic-cohomology-dimension) equals 2 dim S_{k+2}(Γ₁(N)) by the dimension formula; so the injective map is bijective.

Hecke compatibility: Wiese Proposition 7.24 (the Hecke operators on H¹ match slash operators through the period integrals), and ⟨d⟩ likewise; the ± statements follow as in Wiese Corollary 7.33 by dimension.
Descent to general Γ: apply symbols-level-descent with the Γ/Γ′-action, over ℂ.
acceptance: Γ₀(11), k = 0: H¹_par(Γ₀(11), ℂ) is two-dimensional and S₂(Γ₀(11)) one-dimensional.
Level one, weight 12 (k = 10): H¹_par(SL₂(ℤ), V₁₀(ℂ))^± are one-dimensional, spanned by the images of Δ.
The map on the Eisenstein part: Eis_Γ(V_k(ℂ)) corresponds to Eisenstein series (Wiese Theorem 1.9(a)), not used here.

nodes.statement: Let f ∈ S_{k+2}(Γ₁(N)) be a newform of level N with character ε and coefficient field K_f = ℚ(a_n(f), ε). nodes.title: Period lines and periods
nodes.statement: Let f ∈ S_{k+2}(Γ₁(N)) be a normalized newform with character ε_N and coefficient field K_f = ℚ(a_n(f), ε_N), with a fixed embedding K_f ↪ ℂ. For each sign ± the period line is L_f^± := Symb_{Γ₁(N)}(V_k(K_f))^±[λ_f], a one-dimensional K_f-space (L0/eigenspace-dimension), and ψ_f^± := (1 ± ι)ψ_f lies in L_f^± ⊗_{K_f} ℂ. A period exists only after a basis is chosen: for φ^± ∈ L_f^± ∖ {0}, Ω_f^±(φ^±) ∈ ℂ^× is the scalar with ψ_f^± = Ω_f^±(φ^±)·φ^±. Replacing φ^± by λφ^± (λ ∈ K_f^×) replaces Ω_f^± by λ^{−1}Ω_f^± and every period-normalized value by λ times itself.

nodes.title: Saturated integral lattices and integral periods
nodes.statement: Let 𝒪 be a discrete valuation ring (or a PID) whose fraction field K contains K_f, for example the completion of 𝒪_{K_f} at a prime. Let V_k(𝒪) = 𝒪[X, Y]_k with L0's right action. The saturated lattice L_f^±(𝒪) := (L_f^± ⊗_{K_f} K) ∩ Symb_{Γ₁(N)}(V_k(𝒪)) is free of rank one over 𝒪. A generator φ_𝒪^± is unique up to 𝒪^×, so the integral period Ω_{f,𝒪}^± := Ω_f^±(φ_𝒪^±) is canonical up to 𝒪^×. It depends on the lattice V_k(𝒪) (L0/polynomial-duality: V_k(𝒪) and Hom(Sym^k 𝒪², 𝒪) agree only after inverting k!). Comparisons with integral Hecke modules (freeness of the f-part over 𝕋_𝔪, congruence modules) need multiplicity-one hypotheses, which are not assumed here.
hypotheses: Finite generation of Symb_Γ(V_k(𝒪)) comes from Manin's theorem (Div⁰ is finitely generated over ℤ[Γ]; requested from Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 8 by L0).
Multiplicity one enters only when φ_𝒪^± is compared with a generator of a Hecke-module structure; the saturation itself exists for any line.
proofSteps: Symb_Γ(V_k(𝒪)) is finitely generated and torsion-free, and embeds in Symb_Γ(V_k(K)) (symbols-base-change, 𝒪 → K flat).
The intersection of a K-line with it is nonzero (clear denominators of a K_f-basis) and finitely generated torsion-free of rank one, hence free over the PID 𝒪.
Saturation: the quotient of Symb_Γ(V_k(𝒪)) by L_f^±(𝒪) is torsion-free by construction, and generators differ by 𝒪^×.
acceptance: k = 0, 𝒪 = ℤ_(p): φ_𝒪^± is the ℤ_(p)-valued symbol in the line whose values are not all divisible by p.
The non-saturated sublattice p·L_f^±(𝒪) gives a period off by p, not by a unit.
For p ≤ k, V_k(𝒪) and Hom(Sym^k 𝒪², 𝒪) can give different saturations: the pairing of L0/polynomial-duality has denominators C(k, i).

nodes.title: The twisted Mellin formula for modular symbols
nodes.statement: Let f = Σ a_n q^n ∈ S_{k+2}(Γ₁(N)), χ a primitive Dirichlet character of conductor m ≥ 1, τ(χ) = Σ_{a mod m} χ(a)e^{2πia/m}, L(f, χ, s) = Σ χ(n)a_n n^{−s} (entire, in the convention of Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 7), and 0 ≤ j ≤ k. Then, along vertical paths, Σ_{a mod m} χ(a)·2πi∫_{i∞}^{a/m} f(z)(z − a/m)^j dz = τ(χ)·j!/(−2πi)^j·L(f, χ̄, j+1). Equivalently, with χ̄ for χ, Σ_a χ̄(a)·2πi∫_{i∞}^{a/m} f(z)(z − a/m)^j dz = τ(χ̄)·j!/(−2πi)^j·L(f, χ, j+1). In symbol form, Σ_a χ(a)·λ_{j,a/m}(ψ_f({a/m} − {∞})) = τ(χ)·j!/(−2πi)^j·L(f, χ̄, j+1) with λ_{j,x}(P) = (j!/k!)(∂_Y^{k−j}P)(1, −x). For m = 1: 2πi∫_{i∞}^0 f(z)z^j dz = j!/(−2πi)^j·L(f, j+1).
hypotheses: The Mellin transform, entire continuation of L(g, s) for cusp forms g, and twisted L-functions are imported from Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 7 (RS-08).

Every convention that changes the formula is explicit. The sum against χ(a) produces L(f, χ̄), not L(f, χ). The Gauss sum is τ(χ) = Σχ(a)e^{2πia/m}. The path runs from i∞ to a/m; reversing it changes the sign. Using −a/m multiplies by χ(−1). The factor 2πi sits in ψ_f, with j!/(−2πi)^j on the right, and not (2πi)^{j+1}.
proofSteps: Birch's lemma: Σ_{a mod m} χ̄(a)e^{2πina/m} = χ(n)τ(χ̄) for primitive χ and every n, so f_χ := Σχ(n)a_n q^n = τ(χ̄)^{−1}Σ_a χ̄(a) f(z + a/m).

Mellin: for a cusp form g, 2πi∫_{i∞}^{0} g(z)z^j dz = −2πi·i^{j+1}∫_0^∞ g(iy)y^j dy = −2πi·i^{j+1}·j!(2π)^{−j−1}L(g, j+1) = j!/(−2πi)^j·L(g, j+1). The integral converges at both ends because g vanishes at every cusp.
Apply this to g = f_χ and substitute w = z + a/m: Σ_a χ̄(a)·2πi∫_{i∞}^{a/m} f(w)(w − a/m)^j dw = τ(χ̄)·j!/(−2πi)^j·L(f, χ, j+1). Then exchange χ and χ̄.
Symbol form: λ_{j,x}((zX + Y)^k) = (j!/k!)·(k!/j!)(z − x)^j = (z − x)^j.
acceptance: Numerical check with PARI/GP 2.17.2 via cypari2, 2026-09-28, for the characters of order 3 and 6 modulo 7. For 11a1 (k = 0), with the integrals computed through Γ₀(11)-periods, both sides agree to 10^{−14}. For the level-5 weight-4 newform (k = 2) and j = 0, 1, 2, they agree to 10^{−11}. The reading with L(f, χ, j+1) fails by O(1).
For real χ the distinction between χ and χ̄ disappears, so quadratic-twist checks cannot detect a misplaced bar.

nodes.statement: Let T_{j,χ}(ψ) := Σ_{a mod m} χ(a)·λ_{j,a/m}(ψ({a/m} − {∞})) and ε := (−1)^{k−j}χ(−1). Then T_{j,χ}(ψ|ι) = εT_{j,χ}(ψ), so T_{j,χ} vanishes on the −ε eigenspace and T_{j,χ}(ψ_f) = ½T_{j,χ}(ψ_f^ε). For any basis φ^ε of L_f^ε, τ(χ)·j!/(−2πi)^j·L(f, χ̄, j+1)/Ω_f^ε(φ^ε) = ½T_{j,χ}(φ^ε) ∈ K_f(χ), for 0 ≤ j ≤ k and χ primitive. In the dictionary of twisted-mellin-formula, put I_j(x) := 2πi∫_{i∞}^{x} f(z)(z − x)^j dz. For n ≥ 1 the right side equals exactly (−1)^{j+1}/(2πi·Ω_f^±)·α_p^{−n}p^{nj}Σ_{a mod p^n}χ(a)I_j(a/p^n), and equally −ε(−1)^k/(2πi·Ω_f^±)·α_p^{−n}p^{nj}Σ_aχ(a)I_j(−a/p^n), where ε = (−1)^{k−j}χ(−1). So B.1 holds with a j-independent period Ω_f^± exactly when the distribution is normalized through the cusps −a/p^n, or equivalently through x ↦ −x: this is the normalization L2 must fix. nodes.title: Refinements and their slopes
nodes.statement: A refinement at p of a newform f of weight k + 2, level N and character ε is a pair (f, α) with: if p ∤ N, α a root of X² − a_pX + ε(p)p^{k+1}, with refined form f_α (p-stabilisation); if p | N, α = a_p(f) ≠ 0 and refined form f itself. Its slope is h := v_p(α) for a fixed embedding ℚ̄ ↪ ℚ̄_p. The refinement has small slope if h < k + 1 = w − 1, and critical slope if h = k + 1. A refinement is the chosen root together with its eigenline (refined-eigenline); it is not determined by f alone.
hypotheses: Throughout, Γ₀ := Γ₁(N) ∩ Γ₀(p) when p ∤ N and Γ₀ := Γ₁(N) when p | N. Pollack–Stevens work with Γ₀ = Γ ∩ Γ₀(p) for Γ of level prime to p. Their proofs use only that Γ₀ ⊆ Σ₀(p) has finite index (for Corollary 2.10, here L0/symbols-generator-values) and that U_p = Σ_{a=0}^{p−1}|β(a, p) with β(a, p) = (1 a; 0 p). Both hold for Γ₁(N) with p | N (L0/hecke-operators-gamma1), which is the stage's case of p dividing the level.
α is an algebraic integer, so h ≥ 0. When p ∤ N, αβ = ε(p)p^{k+1} with β integral gives v_p(α) + v_p(β) = k + 1, so 0 ≤ h ≤ k + 1.

When p | N and a_p ≠ 0, the slope is k/2 in the case p ‖ N with ε of conductor prime to p (a_p² = ε(p)p^k, the bad-prime eigenvalue milestone of Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 4). This is used only in examples.
proofSteps: Well-definedness is immediate; the slope bound is the valuation identity above.
acceptance: p-ordinary f (a_p a p-adic unit, p ∤ N): one refinement of slope 0 and one of slope k + 1, which is critical.
11a1 at p = 3: slopes 0 and 1 (Pollack–Stevens §8).
p | N with a_p = 0 (for example p² | N with ε of conductor prime to p): no refinement.

nodes.title: Distribution modules with the weight-k action
nodes.statement: For r ∈ |ℂ_p^×|, let A[r] be the ℚ_p-Banach algebra of affinoid functions on B[ℤ_p, r] (the points within r of ℤ_p), A(ℤ_p) = lim_{s>0} A[s] and A†(ℤ_p, r) = lim_{s>r} A[s], with continuous duals D(ℤ_p), D[r] and D†(ℤ_p, r); write D = D[1] and D† = D†(ℤ_p, 1). For r < p, Σ₀(p) := {(a b; c d) ∈ M₂(ℤ_p) : p ∤ a, p | c, ad − bc ≠ 0} acts on A[r] by (γ ·_k f)(z) = (a + cz)^k f((b + dz)/(a + cz)), and on distributions on the right by (μ|_kγ)(f) = μ(γ ·_k f). The resulting modules are D_k(ℤ_p), D_k and D†_k. Moments: μ ↦ (μ(z^j))_j identifies D† with the sequences that are O(r^j) for every r > 1, and D, as a Banach space, with the bounded sequences. For r < p, γ ∈ Σ₀(p) with det γ = p^n and μ ∈ D[r], ‖μ|γ‖_{r/p^n} ≤ ‖μ‖_r.
hypotheses: The spaces A[r], D[r], D(ℤ_p) and their topologies are requested from LocallyAnalyticDistributions L0; the weight-k action and the moment description are built here.
The restriction r < p is needed: for r ≥ p the formula does not preserve A[r] (sourceIssues E8). Every space the stage uses has r ≤ 1 or r slightly above 1.
proofSteps: Proposition 3.1: |μ(z^j)| ≤ ‖z^j‖_r‖μ‖_r = r^j‖μ‖_r gives the growth; conversely, a sequence of that growth defines μ(Σ a_jz^j) := Σ a_jc_j on A†(ℤ_p, 1), since f ∈ A[r] for some r > 1. On D, ‖μ‖_1 = sup_j |μ(z^j)|.

Action and contraction: for r < p and z ∈ B[ℤ_p, r], |cz| < 1 when |z| ≤ max(1, r), so a + cz is a unit and (a + cz)^k has absolute value 1. For z₀ ∈ ℤ_p and |w| ≤ r, |γ(z₀ + w) − γz₀| = |det γ|·|w|/|(a + cz₀)(a + c(z₀ + w))| = p^{−n}|w|, and γz₀ ∈ ℤ_p. So γ maps B[ℤ_p, r] into B[ℤ_p, r/p^n], f ↦ γ ·_k f maps A[r/p^n] into A[r] with norm at most 1, and dualising gives the bound used in the proof of Lemma 6.2.
acceptance: The Dirac distribution δ₀ has moments (1, 0, 0, …) and lies in D.
c_j = 1/(j + 1) is O(r^j) for every r > 1 but unbounded (|1/p^m|_p = p^m), so it defines an element of D† not in D; such denominators are why Theorem 4.5 needs D† (Remark 4.6).
c_j = p^{−j} is not O(r^j) for 1 < r < p, so it is the moment sequence of no element of D†.

nodes.statement: ρ*_k : Symb_{Γ₀}(D†_k) → Symb_{Γ₀}(V_k) is surjective, by an explicit lift of the values on the generators. For μ ∈ D†_k, μ|β(a, p) ∈ D_k, so U_p maps Symb_{Γ₀}(D†_k) into Symb_{Γ₀}(D_k). Hence ρ*_k : Symb_{Γ₀}(D_k) → Symb_{Γ₀}(V_k) is surjective.

The generator-and-relation description is L0/symbols-generator-values, with the D_∞ relation of sourceIssues E1. Pollack–Stevens' proof of Theorem 5.1 uses the printed relation (µ∞|Δ = ν∞); it works verbatim with ν∞ replaced by −ν∞.

By von Staudt–Clausen and Proposition 3.1 it lies in D†_k. Uniqueness is Lemma 4.3.

Theorem 5.1: lift φ(D_i) arbitrarily, lift φ(D′_i) and φ(D″_i) through the idempotents of Proposition 4.1 (2 and 3 are invertible on the ℚ_p-space D†_k), and solve for the value at D_∞ with the difference equation. nodes.title: Slope decomposition of the fibre of specialisation
nodes.statement: Let ϕ ∈ Symb_{Γ₀}(V_k) ⊗ K be a Hecke eigensymbol, K/ℚ_p finite, with U_p-eigenvalue λ of slope h, and X_ϕ := (ρ*_k)^{−1}(K·ϕ) ⊆ Symb_{Γ₀}(D_k) ⊗ K. Then X_ϕ = X_ϕ^{(=h)} ⊕ X_ϕ^{(>h)} uniquely, with u := λ^{−1}U_p topologically nilpotent on X_ϕ^{(>h)}, invertible on X_ϕ^{(=h)} with (u^{−n}) bounded, X_ϕ^{(=h)} finite-dimensional over K, and projection x ↦ lim_n u^{n!}x.
hypotheses: The general statement (Pollack–Stevens Lemma 5.5 and Proposition 5.6: a completely continuous operator preserving a bounded lattice splits the space into a finite-dimensional part where it is invertible and a topologically nilpotent part) is a special case of the Riesz theory of LocallyAnalyticDistributions L4 (finite-slope-summands, riesz-root-projectors); either route may be formalised.

Complete continuity of U_p on Symb_{Γ₀}(D_k): each |β(a, p) maps D[1] into D[1/p] (weight-k-distributions), and the natural map D[1/p] → D[1] is dual to the completely continuous restriction A[1] → A[1/p] (Pollack–Stevens §3.1).
proofSteps: Lattice: Y_ϕ := {Φ in the unit ball of X_ϕ : |Φ(D)(z^j)| ≤ p^{−(h−j)} for 0 ≤ j ≤ ⌊h⌋ and all D ∈ Δ₀}.

u preserves Y_ϕ: (Φ|u)(D)(z^r) = λ^{−1}Σ_a Σ_j C(r, j)a^{r−j}p^jΦ(D_a)(z^j) with D_a = β(a, p)D, and each |p^jΦ(D_a)(z^j)| ≤ p^{−h} (by the defining bound for j ≤ ⌊h⌋ and because j > h otherwise), so |(Φ|u)(D)(z^r)| ≤ 1. Membership in Y_ϕ depends only on ρ*_k(Φ), and ρ*_k(Φ|u) = ρ*_k(Φ).
The unit ball itself need not be u-stable (Pollack–Stevens' footnote (3)), which is why Y_ϕ is used.
Apply the lattice decomposition (Proposition 5.6) to u on X_ϕ.
acceptance: h = 0: Y_ϕ is the whole unit ball, and the projector is Hida's ordinary projector lim U_p^{n!} up to the unit λ.
X_ϕ is infinite-dimensional (it contains ker ρ*_k), while X_ϕ^{(=h)} is finite-dimensional.
For h > 0 the unit ball of X_ϕ need not be preserved by u.

nodes.title: Stevens' control theorem in small slope
nodes.statement: Specialisation induces isomorphisms Symb_{Γ₀}(D_k(ℤ_p))^{(<k+1)} ≅ Symb_{Γ₀}(D_k)^{(<k+1)} ≅ Symb_{Γ₀}(V_k)^{(<k+1)} of the subspaces on which U_p acts with slope < k + 1, compatible with the Hecke operators and ι. In particular, for a refinement (f, α) of slope h < k + 1 and each basis φ^± of the refined eigenline, there is a unique Φ^± ∈ Symb_{Γ₀}(D_k(ℤ_p))^± with ρ*_k(Φ^±) = φ^±, and Φ^± is a Hecke eigensymbol with the eigenvalues of f_α.
hypotheses: Throughout, Γ₀ := Γ₁(N) ∩ Γ₀(p) when p ∤ N and Γ₀ := Γ₁(N) when p | N. Pollack–Stevens work with Γ₀ = Γ ∩ Γ₀(p) for Γ of level prime to p. Their proofs use only that Γ₀ ⊆ Σ₀(p) has finite index (for Corollary 2.10, here L0/symbols-generator-values) and that U_p = Σ_{a=0}^{p−1}|β(a, p) with β(a, p) = (1 a; 0 p). Both hold for Γ₁(N) with p | N (L0/hecke-operators-gamma1), which is the stage's case of p dividing the level.

Pollack–Stevens cite the first isomorphism (independence of the radius on the finite-slope part) to their critical-slope preprint [16, Lemma 5.2], which was not read. Here it is derived from the contraction of weight-k-distributions. For Φ in the finite-slope part of Symb_{Γ₀}(D_k) (finite-dimensional by the Riesz theory), Φ = (Φ|U_p^{−n})|U_p^n with Φ|U_p^{−n} in the same space, and |U_p^n = Σ_{a mod p^n}|β(a, p^n) maps D[1]-valued symbols to D[1/p^n]-valued ones. So Φ takes values in every D[1/p^n], hence in D(ℤ_p) = lim_s D[s] (the maps D[s] → D[1] are injective).

Surjectivity (Theorem 5.9 with Lemma 5.10): for an eigensymbol ϕ of slope h, ρ*_k maps X_ϕ^{(=h)} onto K·ϕ (overconvergent-lift, slope-decomposition-fibre; ρ*_k kills X_ϕ^{(>h)}). When h < k + 1 this map is also injective, so the eigensymbol it produces lifts a nonzero multiple of ϕ.
An isomorphism after extending scalars to ℚ̄_p is one before.
Uniqueness of Φ^± and its eigen-property follow from the Hecke-equivariant isomorphism and the one-dimensionality of the refined eigenline.
acceptance: h = 0: Hida's ordinary control theorem for Γ₀.

At h = k + 1 specialisation can fail to be an isomorphism on the f-part: by Theorem 5.14 it fails exactly for f in the image of θ_k, which includes the critical-slope stabilisation of a p-ordinary CM form (Remark 5.15). That is stage L3.
The threshold is strict: slope k + 1 = w − 1 is excluded.

nodes.title: Interpolation and uniqueness of the p-adic L-function
nodes.statement: Let (f, α) have slope h < k + 1, with φ^± and Ω^± as in p-adic-l-function, 0 ≤ j ≤ k, and χ a character of ℤ_p^× of conductor p^n. With ± := (−1)^jχ(−1), L_p(f, α; φ^±)(z^j·χ) = e·α^{−n}p^{nj}·τ(χ)·j!/(2πi)^j·L(f_α, χ^{−1}, j + 1)/Ω^±, where e = 1 if n ≥ 1 and e = 1 − p^j/α if n = 0 (χ trivial). For p ∤ N and n = 0, L(f_α, j + 1) = (1 − ε(p)p^{k−j}/α)L(f, j + 1) supplies the second Euler factor. In L1's notation I_j(x) = 2πi∫_{i∞}^x f_α(z)(z − x)^j dz, the right side for n ≥ 1 is ±α^{−n}p^{nj}Σ_{a mod p^n}χ(a)I_j(−a/p^n)/Ω^±. This is RJW Theorem B.1 with Ω_{B.1}^± = −Ω^±/(2πi), a j-independent conversion. Moreover, L_p(f, α; φ^±) is the unique h-admissible distribution on ℤ_p^× with these values, because h < k + 1.
hypotheses: Pollack–Stevens (1) prints the formula as α^{−n}p^{n(j+1)}/(−2πi)^j·j!/τ(χ^{−1})·L(f, χ^{−1}, j+1)/Ω^±. It agrees with (2), and hence with Proposition 6.3, only up to the sign ± (sourceIssues E4), and it omits e at n = 0 (sourceIssues E5). The statement here is the one (2) implies.

Uniqueness of an h-admissible distribution from its values on locally polynomial functions of degree ≤ k when h < k + 1 (Amice–Vélu, Višik) is requested from LocallyAnalyticDistributions L2. At h = k + 1 it fails (stage L3).
proofSteps: Case n ≥ 1: sum (2) against χ(a) over a mod p^n with p ∤ a. With (−p^nz + a)^j = (−p^n)^j(z − a/p^n)^j and (p^nz + a)^j = p^{nj}(z + a/p^n)^j, the ±-part is α^{−n}p^{nj}[(−1)^jS ± Σ_aχ(a)I_j(−a/p^n)]/(2Ω^±), where S := Σ_aχ(a)I_j(a/p^n). Substituting a ↦ −a gives Σ_aχ(a)I_j(−a/p^n) = χ(−1)S, so the ±-part vanishes unless ± = (−1)^jχ(−1), and then equals α^{−n}p^{nj}(−1)^jS/Ω^±.
L1/twisted-mellin-formula: S = τ(χ)·j!/(−2πi)^j·L(f_α, χ̄, j + 1), which gives the formula with e = 1.

Case n = 0: L_p(z^j) = Φ({∞} − {0})(z^j) − Φ({∞} − {0})(z^j·1_{pℤ_p}), and by the distribution relation with a = 0, n = 1 the second term is α^{−1}p^jΦ({∞} − {0})(z^j). So L_p(z^j) = (1 − p^j/α)·Φ({∞} − {0})(z^j), and the case a = 0, n = 0 of the computation above evaluates Φ({∞} − {0})(z^j). L1/p-stabilised-euler-factors converts L(f_α, j + 1).

RJW comparison: L1/rjw-b1-comparison writes B.1's right side as −ε(−1)^k/(2πi·Ω_{B.1})·α^{−n}p^{nj}Σ_aχ(a)I_j(−a/p^n) with ε = (−1)^{k−j}χ(−1), so ε(−1)^k = (−1)^jχ(−1) = ±. Comparing with the formula above gives Ω_{B.1}^± = −Ω^±/(2πi).

Uniqueness: two h-admissible distributions with h < k + 1 that agree on locally polynomial functions of degree ≤ k are equal (LAD L2). The values on z^j·1_{a+p^nℤ_p}, given by (2), determine L_p on such functions.
acceptance: k = 0, n = 0, p ∤ N, trivial ε: L_p(1) = (1 − 1/α)²·L(f, 1)/Ω^+, the Mazur–Tate–Teitelbaum shape.
For quadratic χ, and on the +-part, (1) as printed and (2) agree; only the −-part carries the sign of E4.

nodes.title: Ordinary p-adic L-functions as integral measures
nodes.statement: Let (f, α) have slope 0, 𝒪 the integers of a finite extension K of ℚ_p containing K_f(α), and φ^± generators of the saturated lattices L_{f,α}^±(𝒪) := L_{f,α}^± ∩ Symb_{Γ₀}(V_k(𝒪)). Then L_p(f, α; φ^±) is a measure with values in 𝒪: for p ∤ a, L_p(1_{a+p^nℤ_p}) = α^{−n}·[Y^k](φ({∞} − {a/p^n})) ∈ 𝒪, where φ := φ⁺ + φ⁻ and [Y^k] is the Y^k-coefficient. So L_p ∈ 𝒪⟦ℤ_p^×⟧. Boundedness alone, that is h = 0 with arbitrary bases φ^±, gives only an element of 𝒪⟦ℤ_p^×⟧[1/p].
hypotheses: The saturated lattice of a line and its generator, unique up to 𝒪^×, are L1/integral-period-lattices. Its proof uses only that the line lies in Symb_{Γ₀}(V_k(K)) for a finite-index Γ₀, so it applies to the refined eigenline.
The identification of 0-admissible distributions with bounded measures, K ⊗ 𝒪⟦ℤ_p^×⟧, is requested from LocallyAnalyticDistributions L2 (order zero).
proofSteps: Distribution relation with g = 1: L_p(1_{a+p^nℤ_p}) = α^{−n}Φ({∞} − {a/p^n})(1), and Φ(D)(1) is the Y^k-coefficient of ρ_k(Φ(D)) = φ(D) (specialisation-map), with no binomial denominator.

α ∈ 𝒪^× and φ(D) ∈ V_k(𝒪), so every value on a compact open is in 𝒪. By eigensymbol-admissibility L_p is 0-admissible, hence a bounded measure, and it is determined by its values on compact opens, so it lies in 𝒪⟦ℤ_p^×⟧.
For bases p^{−m}·(integral generator) the values lie in p^{−m}𝒪.
acceptance: 11a1 at p = 3 with the unit root α ∈ ℤ_3^× of X² + X + 3 (≡ −1 mod 3 by Hensel): L_p ∈ ℤ_3⟦ℤ_3^×⟧ for the integral generators φ^±.
p^{−1}φ^± in place of φ^± gives a bounded measure in p^{−1}𝒪⟦ℤ_p^×⟧, in general not in 𝒪⟦ℤ_p^×⟧.
For the moments μ(z^j) with 1 ≤ j ≤ k no integrality follows from φ ∈ V_k(𝒪) alone: ρ_k involves the binomials C(k, j), which can be divisible by p when p ≤ k.

nodes.title: The critical-slope p-adic L-function of a non-θ-critical refinement
nodes.statement: Let (f, α) be a refinement of critical slope h = k + 1 (ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L2 refinement) that is not θ-critical (equivalently non-critical, by PadicFamilies L3). Then each refined eigenline φ^± has a unique overconvergent eigen-lift Φ^± ∈ Symb_Γ(D_k)^± with ρ*_k(Φ^±) = φ^±, and L_p(f, α; φ^±) := Φ({∞} − {0})|_{ℤ_p^×} with Φ = Φ⁺ + Φ⁻. It is (k + 1)-admissible, satisfies the distribution relation of L2, and its ±-parts are Bellaïche's L±(f_α, ·) with the scalars fixed by ρ*_k(Φ^±) = φ^± (so the periods Ω^± are those of L2).
hypotheses: Critical slope and not θ-critical; the uniqueness of the lift is Pollack–Stevens' Theorem 5.14 / Bellaïche's Theorem 1 with e = 1 (PadicFamilies L3).
proofSteps: By PadicFamilies L3 (e = 1), ρ*_k restricts to an isomorphism of the f_α-eigenspaces, so the lifts exist and are unique; evaluate at {∞} − {0} as in L2.
Admissibility of order k + 1: the U_p-eigenvalue has valuation k + 1 (Višik's criterion).
acceptance: The normalisation is by specialisation, not by values: at critical slope values do not determine the distribution.

nodes.title: Interpolation does not determine critical-slope L-functions
nodes.statement: At h = k + 1 there are nonzero (k + 1)-admissible distributions on ℤ_p^× vanishing at every z^j·χ (0 ≤ j ≤ k, χ of finite order): for each tame character ψ, the distribution whose Mellin transform in the variable s is log^{[k]}(s) = ∏_{i=0}^{k} log_p(γ^{−i}s). Hence the interpolation values do not determine L_p(f, α; φ^±); its uniqueness is the uniqueness of the eigen-lift, not of an admissible distribution.
hypotheses: Amice–Vélu–Višik uniqueness holds only for h < k + 1 (LocallyAnalyticDistributions L2).
proofSteps: log^{[k]} has order exactly k + 1 and vanishes at s = γ^jζ for all p-power roots of unity ζ and 0 ≤ j ≤ k, which are exactly the images of the characters z^jχ.
Adding a multiple of it to L_p preserves all interpolation values and (k + 1)-admissibility.
acceptance: Do not extend the strict inequality h < k + 1 of the uniqueness theorem by continuity.

nodes.title: Comparing critical and arithmetic L-functions through families
nodes.statement: Let V ∋ x be the affinoid neighbourhood of a decent critical-slope point in the eigencurve with two-variable L±(y, σ) (PadicFamilies L3). If an identity between L±(y, ·) and an arithmetic construction (e.g. Kato's) holds, up to the normalising function of y, at a Zariski-dense set of non-critical classical points y ∈ V, it holds at x; comparisons at x by interpolation values alone are not valid.

nodes.title: p-adic L-functions with a tame twist (Pollack §2.2–2.3)
nodes.statement: Let f be a newform of weight k + 2, level N and character ε, p ∤ N, and (f, α) a refinement of slope h < k + 1. Let M ≥ 1 be prime to p and Z_{p,M}^× = lim_n (Z/p^nM)^×. For (a, Mp) = 1, the formula μ^±_{f,α}(P, a + p^nMZ_{p,M}) = α^{−n}λ^±(f, P; a, p^nM) − ε(p)p^kα^{−n−1}λ^±(f, P; a, p^{n−1}M) defines an h-admissible measure on Z_{p,M}^× (Proposition 2.8). Here λ^± are the modular symbols of f divided by periods Ω^±_f, and P runs over integral polynomials of degree ≤ k. For a tame character ψ, the power series L_p(f, α, ψ, T) = ∫ ψχ_u dμ^{sgn ψ}_{f,α} (u = 1 + T, χ_u the wild character with γ ↦ u) lies in K(α, ψ)[[T]] and is O(log_p(1 + T)^h). Take χ = x_p^jϕ with 0 ≤ j ≤ k and ϕ of finite order and conductor m = p^νM. Then L_p(f, α, χ) = e_p(α, χ)·m^{j+1}/(−2πi)^j·j!/τ(ϕ^{−1})·L(fϕ^{−1}, j + 1)/Ω^±_f, with e_p(α, χ) = α^{−ν}(1 − ϕ^{−1}(p)ε(p)p^{k−j}/α)(1 − ϕ(p)p^j/α). It is the unique O(log_p(1 + T)^h) function with these values (Proposition 2.11). With M = 1 it is the L_p(f, α) of L2/p-adic-l-function, up to the normalisation of periods.

The proof of the interpolation formula is Mazur–Tate–Teitelbaum §14, which is not read; the formula agrees with L2/interpolation-and-uniqueness for M = 1 and with L4/euler-factor-comparison.

Integrate ψχ_u against μ^{sgn ψ} to get an analytic function of u in the open unit disc, O(log^h) by Theorem 2.6.

Evaluate at χ = x_p^jϕ with the twisted Mellin formula (L1/twisted-mellin-formula) to get Proposition 2.11. Uniqueness holds because a difference vanishes at all γ^jζ − 1 (0 ≤ j ≤ k) and is O(log^h) with h < k + 1.

nodes.title: Both refinements at a good supersingular prime, and their zeros (Pollack §3)
nodes.statement: Let p ∤ NM be supersingular for f, so v_p(a_p) > 0. Then both roots α₁, α₂ of X² − a_pX + ε(p)p^{k+1} have slope h_i ∈ (0, k + 1), since h₁ + h₂ = k + 1. So both refinements are small slope, and both L_p(f, α_i, ψ, T) exist. (Mazur, Theorem 3.3) If h₁ ≠ h₂, at least one of them has infinitely many zeros in the open unit disc. (Perrin-Riou, Theorem 3.5) If a_p = 0, then h₁ = h₂ = (k + 1)/2 and α₂ = −α₁. Write L_p(f, α₁, ψ, T) = G⁺_ψ(T) + G⁻_ψ(T)·α₁ with G^± ∈ K(ψ)[[T]]. For odd p, G⁺_ψ vanishes at ζ_{p^{2n}} − 1 and G⁻_ψ at ζ_{p^{2n−1}} − 1 for n ≥ 1; for p = 2 the parities are reversed. One of the two L-functions has infinitely many zeros, and both do if α₁ ∉ K(ψ). (Corollary 3.6) For an elliptic curve E/Q with good supersingular reduction at p, one of the two has infinitely many zeros. For p ≥ 5, a_p = 0, because p | a_p and a_p² < 4p. For p = 2 or 3 with a_p ≠ 0, α₁/α₂ is a primitive fourth or sixth root of unity, which still forces G^± to have infinitely many zeros.
hypotheses: Weights follow this roadmap: f has weight k + 2 (Pollack's k is our k + 2).
A power series convergent on the open unit disc has finitely many zeros exactly when its coefficients are bounded (Lemma 3.2, Lazard).
proofSteps: Remark 2.12: L_p(f, α_i, ψ, ζ_{p^n} − 1) = c_n/α_i^{n+1} with c_n independent of α_i (exponent n + 2 for p = 2).
h₁ ≠ h₂: if both had finitely many zeros they would have bounded coefficients, and comparing valuations of α₁^{n+1}L(α₁) = α₂^{n+1}L(α₂) as n → ∞ contradicts h₁ ≠ h₂.

a_p = 0: α₁ = −α₂ makes the two values agree for odd n and differ by a sign for even n, which forces the zeros of G^±. Bounded G^± cannot have infinitely many zeros, so one L-function is unbounded, hence has infinitely many zeros.
acceptance: Ordinary p is excluded: then only one root has slope < k + 1.
Weight 2 (k = 0) with a_p = 0: both slopes are 1/2.

nodes.title: Pollack's half-logarithms log^±_p (§4)
nodes.statement: Let γ generate 1 + qZ_p (q = p, or 4 if p = 2) and Φ_n(T) = Σ_{t=0}^{p−1} T^{p^{n−1}t}, the p^n-th cyclotomic polynomial. nodes.title: Rational separation of parabolic and boundary Hecke supports
nodes.statement: Let N ≥ 3 and k ≥ 0, H = H¹(Γ(N), V_k(ℚ)) and P = H¹_par(Γ(N), V_k(ℚ)). Let T be the ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(H) generated by the usual good-prime T_ℓ and scalar S_ℓ, for primes ℓ not dividing N, transported through the polynomial-coefficient dictionary. There exist A ∈ T and coprime polynomials F,G ∈ ℚ[X] such that F(A) vanishes on P and the image of G(A) lies in P, equivalently G(A) vanishes on H/P. These are annihilators, not just a statement about individual eigenvectors.
hypotheses: The finite-dimensional rational cohomology and parabolic subspace are those of the existing L0 nodes, with the connected full-level carrier Γ(N).
The usual cohomological Hecke normalization and its transport to the adjugate polynomial action must be proved; the full-level comparison is recorded as an open request.
proofSteps: In weight two use Elkik §III: choose a prime ℓ congruent to 1 modulo N; T_ℓ acts on the boundary quotient by ℓ+1, while every cusp-form eigenvalue has absolute value strictly smaller than ℓ+1. Elkik proves the strict bound by the Petersson norm triangle inequality and the Fourier-expansion obstruction to equality, without Deligne’s theorem.

Transport the cusp-form bound to parabolic cohomology through Eichler–Shimura. Cayley–Hamilton gives rational annihilators and the absence of a shared root gives their coprimality. The native Nat.exists_prime_gt_modEq_one supplies the congruence prime by its cyclotomic argument; it is not a statement about every good prime.

For higher weight Sharifi Theorem 3.4.16 cites the rational left-kernel theorem of Shokurov. Its cohomological transport, together with the separation of cusp and Eisenstein Hecke characters, must furnish separating rational annihilators in the finite good Hecke algebra. The unread source step is recorded as a gap; Elkik’s trivial-local-system proof is not asserted to cover k > 0.
acceptance: The conditions on F and G control generalized eigenspaces, so a nonsemisimple boundary extension is included.
In weight two the boundary scalar ℓ+1 and Elkik’s strict cusp bound imply that X−(ℓ+1) is coprime to the parabolic characteristic polynomial.
Annihilator separation is over ℚ. It gives no coprimality over ℤ at a congruence prime.

nodes.title: The rational Drinfeld–Manin splitting
nodes.statement: For N ≥ 3 and k ≥ 0 there is a unique ℚ-linear retraction s_N : H¹(Γ(N),V_k(ℚ)) → H¹_par(Γ(N),V_k(ℚ)) equivariant for the rational good Hecke algebra (usual T_ℓ and scalar S_ℓ, ℓ not dividing N). Its inclusion-composite is the rational parabolic projector. Under the requested coefficient/local-system comparison, take the direct sum over geometric components to obtain Nakamura’s s_N : H¹(Y(N)(ℂ),𝒱_{k+2/ℚ}) → H¹(X(N)(ℂ),j_*𝒱_{k+2/ℚ}). Rationalization precedes this construction; no integral splitting is asserted.
hypotheses: Nakamura’s weight is k+2 and his curve Y(N) has all geometric components, whereas the connected Betti prototype uses Γ(N).

The comparison between Nakamura’s dual symmetric-power local system and the packet’s adjugate action, including determinant twists and usual versus adjoint Hecke operators, is requested from the geometric supplier.
Higher-weight rational spectral separation has the source gap recorded at rational-hecke-separation.
proofSteps: Take A,F,G from rational-hecke-separation and Bézout polynomials a,b with aF+bG=1. Set e=b(A)G(A). Its image lies in P and it restricts to the identity on P, since F(A) kills P. Native projection theory identifies ker(e) as a complement.
Every good Hecke generator commutes with A, hence with e. Restrict the codomain of e to P to define s_N. This supplies existence, retraction, equivariance and idempotence.
If t is another Hecke-equivariant retraction, it commutes with A and all its polynomials. Since F(A) kills P, t(1−e)=a(A)|_P F(A)|_P t=0, while t e=s_N. Therefore t=s_N.
For an endomorphism preserving P and commuting with the good Hecke algebra, its commutation with the same polynomial projector proves naturality.

After the requested geometric dictionary, the usual and adjoint Hecke actions are related by Nakamura Lemma 3.1, with T′_ℓ=ℓ^k T_ℓ S_ℓ⁻¹ and S′_ℓ=ℓ^(2k) S_ℓ⁻¹. Thus the projector commutes with both. The full-curve action of complex conjugation, and the Galois action after rational p-adic coefficient extension and Betti–étale comparison, must be transported through that dictionary; the suggested file does not claim to have these geometric carriers.
acceptance: At full level N=3 and weight two (k=0), X(3) has genus zero, the parabolic subspace is zero and drinfeldManin 3 0 is the zero linear map. Ordinary H¹ has dimension three, so the ordinary and parabolic spaces are not identified.
At full level N=6 and weight two, dim_ℚ H¹_par=2 and s_6 restricts to the identity on that subspace. This excludes the zero retraction.

For H=ℚ², P=ℚ×{0} and T(x,y)=(y,2y), the Bézout projector e=1−T/2 sends (0,1) to (−1/2,0), fixes (1,0), kills T(H), commutes with T and satisfies e²=e. Projection onto the first coordinate alone fails to commute with T.
For the same model over ℤ there is no ℤ-linear retraction s:ℤ²→ℤ with s(1,0)=1 and s(Tv)=0 for all v: substituting v=(0,1) forces 1+2s(0,1)=0.
